projectile.about: Projectile thrown at an angle; trail and velocity arrow; vertical and horizontal components differ.
projectile.hint: camera distance about 14 to show a 10 unit range in explainer_window; plot vy with sim(3,0,X); flight time is 2 vy / g, so a beat of 4 s fits vy up to about 10 m/s at timeScale 1

incline_sliding.about: Block sliding down an incline of angle 30 degrees with friction mu: a = g(sin - mu cos).
incline_sliding.hint: for an incline from (0,h) down to (L cos a, 0) place the block at the top; surface is drawn automatically. Place the block centre half its height above the surface; the block slides s = 1/2 a t^2 (about 3.2 m/s^2 here), so pick timeScale so it reaches the bottom inside the beat; add a floor segment at the end so it stops there

rolling_race.about: A disc and a block (or a ring) start together on the same incline; the rolling one is slower because some energy goes into rotation.
rolling_race.hint: balls need friction mu >= 0.5 to roll; give ring bodies kind 'ring' (I = m r^2); put them on different heights/rails or in separate scenes

pendulum.about: Simple pendulum on a rod or rope; period T = 2 pi sqrt(L/g).
pendulum.hint: start position must be at distance length from the pivot: pos = pivot + L (sin a, -cos a). The rod is drawn automatically; add a small sphere at the pivot (and a ceiling box) yourself

spring_mass.about: Mass on a spring oscillating on a frictionless floor: T = 2 pi sqrt(m/k).
spring_mass.hint: the spring coil is drawn automatically between the anchor and the block; draw a wall at the anchor yourself. For the x-t graph plot sim(0,0,X) - 2 (displacement from equilibrium at x = L0 = 2); T = 2 pi sqrt(m/k)

collision_1d.about: Two carts colliding on a frictionless track; restitution 1 is elastic, 0 is perfectly inelastic; momentum is conserved.
collision_1d.hint: set gravity [0,0] for a track; add a thin box object as the track; compare e = 1 and e = 0 in two beats

atwood.about: Two masses over a pulley: a = (m1 - m2) g / (m1 + m2), tension T = 2 m1 m2 g / (m1 + m2).
atwood.hint: rope length = vertical strand lengths at the start: (pulley y - m1 y) + (pulley y - m2 y). The rope is drawn automatically; draw the pulley with the pulley_wheel prefab at the pulley point; with m1 = 2 and m2 = 1 the heavier mass falls 1/2 a t^2: keep both masses between the floor and the pulley during the beat by using timeScale

circular_motion.about: Ball on a string moving in a vertical circle or a horizontal path: centripetal acceleration v^2/r.
circular_motion.hint: use gravity [0,0] for a flat circle; initial velocity perpendicular to the string; a = v^2/r points to the centre

orbit.about: A planet orbiting a heavy star under inverse-square gravity: v = sqrt(GM/r), T = 2 pi sqrt(r^3/GM).
orbit.hint: circular orbit needs v = sqrt(G M / r); v larger gives an ellipse; draw the star with a sphere object bound by `bind`

charge_in_B.about: Charged particle in a uniform magnetic field moves in a circle of radius m v / (q B).
charge_in_B.hint: B out of the screen is positive; the force direction is q v x B
